script.text: Good morning! I'm Kelly, and this is your daily lesson for February 8. Today we're exploring two powerful ideas together.

The rain falling today is ancient.  The same water has been cycling from ocean to sky to land and back for billions of years.  The drop that lands on your window might have fallen on dinosaurs, filled Roman baths, flowed through countless rivers.

Sun heats ocean water, which evaporates—becoming invisible vapor. The vapor rises, cools, and condenses into tiny droplets around dust particles. Those droplets form clouds. When enough droplets merge, they become heavy enough to fall. Rain. Earth's water is a closed system—essentially no new water is created or destroyed.  The water you drink has been through countless cycles: ocean, atmosphere, glacier, river, plant, animal.
Today's wisdom: Here's today's wisdom: Rain reminds us that we're part of cycles larger than ourselves.  The water in your body will one day be clouds, rivers, oceans.
Now let's take what we learned and put it into practice.
Today's growth challenge is Cycle Awareness - See the System.

Here's your activity: Follow water today: drink a glass and trace where it might have been—ocean, cloud, river, reservoir, tap. Then trace where it will go next. You're a waystation in an endless cycle. This helps you recognize the cycles you participate in.
And here's how today's lessons connect: What you learned about where rain comes from can be applied to cycle awareness - see the system. Practice makes progress.
That's today's lesson. Learn something, grow a little. I'll see you tomorrow with something new. Stay curious!
